chunks: The Shaykh, the jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil b. Salih from Muhammad b. Marwan. He said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) saying:

Surely, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has in every night of the month of Ramadan freed ones and released ones from the Fire, except whoever breaks their fast on an intoxicant. And when it is the last night of it, He frees in it the like of what He freed in all of it.

key_terms.عتقاء: freed ones, those liberated from Hellfire

ai.seo_question: What does Islam teach about Allah freeing people from Hellfire during Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), delivered during a Ramadan assembly in 367 AH, emphasizes Allah's immense mercy during the blessed month. It teaches that God frees souls from Hellfire every night of Ramadan, with the last night being especially momentous as He frees as many as in the entire month combined. The sole exception is those who break their fast with intoxicants, underscoring the severity of consuming alcohol during this sacred period.
word_analysis: may Allah have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (rh) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa`id from Ibn Abi `Umayr from Jamil b. Salih from Muhammad b. Marwan. He said: I heard al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) say:

Surely, for every night in the month of Ramadan, Allah frees people from the Fire; except for those who break their fast on an intoxicant. On the last night of it, He frees as many people as He frees in the rest of the month.
